propositions: Closing a ticket invokes _compact_on_close which acquires the store write lock and holds it for the entire compaction fold (git commit, snapshot write, source retire), causing multi-minute lock holds (measured up to 13m53s) that block all concurrent agent writes.

The store write lock hold during compact-on-close is unbounded and unmonitored; nested git operations through gitutil.run_git_write add advisory flocks and retry budgets that stack inside the held lock, compounding contention.

Compaction is optional housekeeping for performance and storage size, not a correctness requirement; unfolded event logs remain valid and reducible, so removing the close-path trigger changes performance characteristics only.

The solution is to remove _compact_on_close and its call site from transition_close.py, allowing closes to complete in seconds rather than minutes, while keeping the manual rebar compact CLI and a follow-up out-of-band sweep trigger intact.
